title: Local versus global optimum
summary: A local optimum is best in a neighborhood; a global optimum is best over the entire feasible domain.

context.note: Framework is named textually in this seed release; full recursive first-principles closure remains future work.

assumptions.text: A feasible set, objective, and neighborhood structure are specified.

content.plain: Being unbeatable nearby does not mean being best everywhere.
content.exact: For minimization, x* is a local minimizer if some neighborhood U satisfies f(x*)≤f(x) for all x∈U∩X. It is global if the inequality holds for all x∈X.
content.example: f(x)=(x^2-1)^2+0.1x has distinct local minima of different objective values.
content.caveat: Some problems have no local traps (for example certain convex problems), while others have many. The distinction depends on the feasible geometry and objective.
